title: Add connection
pickHint: Choose the type of database to connect to.

fields.name: Name
fields.projectHint: Saved in the repository's .spelaion/ folder and shared through git. Passwords are never written to it.
fields.personalHint: Saved only on this computer, in your personal settings folder.
fields.noTunnelsHint: No network profiles yet: create one with “New profile…”.
fields.fileHint: An existing file, or a new empty one from “New database…”. Inside the repository the path is stored relative to it.
fields.mcpHint: Agents using spelaiondb mcp can only read, and every query is audited.
fields.mcpWriteHint: Agents can run one write at a time (INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE with WHERE, CREATE or ALTER of tables, views and indexes…), each in its own transaction. DROP, TRUNCATE, changes to every row, procedures and permissions are always refused, and everything is audited.
fields.mcpProdWarning: This connection's type asks before data changes: agents will be able to change its data.
fields.tlsHint: With “Verify”, an empty certificate field uses the system’s trusted certificates.
fields.useTunnel: Connect through a network profile (SSH tunnel or proxy)
fields.tunnelHint: The database is reached from the profile’s last SSH hop, or through its proxy when it has no hops. Profiles are shared: Settings → Network lists them all.
fields.fixedLocationHint: When editing, the connection stays in the same file and folder.
fields.serverFileHint: Its path on the tunnel's last hop. SpelaionDB runs that server's sqlite3 (3.37 or later, in its safe mode): the file is never copied.
fields.useTunnelForFile: The file is on a server: open it there through an SSH tunnel
fields.tunnelForFileHint: The last hop must allow running commands (not only port forwarding) and have sqlite3 installed.
fields.keepaliveHint: A query tab left open sends the server a tiny query after this long without use, so a firewall or the server's idle timeout does not end it overnight. Never while a transaction is open. Empty or 0: off.
fields.connectTimeoutHint: How long the database may take to accept the connection and the login before the attempt fails. Empty: 15 s. A network profile's hops have their own timeout.
fields.statementTimeoutHint: A statement run from the editor that takes longer is cancelled and fails as timed out. Empty or 0: no limit. A run can set its own in the editor.
fields.localPortHint: Fixed port on 127.0.0.1 where the tunnel listens for this connection, so other tools can use it too. Empty: any free port (or one from the range in Settings → Network).
fields.tlsCertPlaceholder: Empty: log in with the authentication method
fields.clientCertHint: Logs in with a certificate instead of a password (the server must accept it for this user). The key stays on your computer: keep it in your personal folder, never in the repository.
fields.label: Label
fields.labelHint: A label of your own only names the connection: it has no color and no safeguards.
fields.descriptionPlaceholder: What is this database for? Who owns it?
fields.descriptionHint: Shown as the connection's tooltip and, if it is exposed, to AI agents, so they know what the database is for. Never put passwords here.
fields.tagsHint: Short labels to find the connection: press Enter or type a comma after each one. Click a tag in the explorer to show only the connections that have it.

tls.prefer: Prefer (encrypt if the server allows it)
tls.verify-full: Verify the authority and the host name

hints.config: The connection or its network profile could not be read: fix what the message names (a variable, a secret reference, a file path).
hints.passwordRequired: This connection asks for its password every time: type it in the form to test the login.
hints.cancelled: A question (a password, a passphrase or a server fingerprint) was dismissed, so the test stopped there. Test again and answer it.
hints.proxyAuth: The proxy refused the username or the password. Check them in the proxy section of the network profile.
hints.sshAuth: This SSH server refused every method tried: check the user, the key (its public key must be in the server's authorized_keys), the password or the agent. Some servers refuse passwords altogether.
hints.hostUnreachable: Nothing answered at this address: check the host name and port, that the server is running, and that this step's network (VPN, firewall, the previous hop) can reach it.
hints.hostKeyChanged: This server's key is not the one stored for it. That happens when a server is reinstalled, and also when someone intercepts the connection. Ask its administrator for its new fingerprint; only once it is confirmed, remove the old line from the known_hosts file the message names. SpelaionDB will not connect to it until then.
hints.hostKeyRejected: The server's fingerprint was not accepted. Compare it with the one its administrator gives you, then test again.
hints.dbAuth: The database refused the user or the password. Check both, and that this user may log in from where the connection arrives (the last hop, with a tunnel).
hints.dbNotFound: The server answered, but the database (or file) does not exist or this user cannot open it: check its name.
hints.tls: The encrypted connection failed: check the SSL/TLS mode, the CA certificate, and that the host name matches the server's certificate (through a tunnel the real server name is still checked).
hints.timeout: No answer in time: the server may be down, or a firewall may be dropping packets. Check the address, or raise the connect timeout if the network is only slow.
hints.kubernetes: kubectl could not forward the port: check the context, namespace, resource and port in the Kubernetes tab, and that kubectl works from a terminal.
hints.other: See the message. Copy the diagnostics to share them: secrets are left out.

auth.savedHint: The password goes to the system keychain (Credential Manager, Keychain or Secret Service), never to the connection file.
auth.askHint: Not saved: it will be asked each time you connect. The password typed here is only used to test.
auth.noKeychainHint: There is no system keychain to save it in (on Linux a Secret Service such as GNOME Keyring, KWallet or KeePassXC must be running): it will be asked each time you connect.
auth.envHint: Read from this variable when connecting; the file only stores its name.
auth.otherHint: This password comes from a reference the form cannot edit (1Password, a command or a named keychain entry). It is kept as is; edit the file to change it.
auth.keepPlaceholder: Leave empty to keep the saved password

filterHint: Patterns separated by commas: * is any run of characters, ? one character, \ escapes the next one; case is ignored. Without include patterns everything is included; exclude patterns hide what matches them.
filterPersonal: Filters are yours: they are saved on this computer, not in the connection's file, and only change what the explorer shows.
deleteExplanation: {{name}} will be removed: its file {{file}} is deleted, along with its password in the system keychain if one was saved.
deleteProjectHint: It is a project connection, shared through git: your team will lose it too when you commit the change.
deletePersonalHint: It is a personal connection: only this computer is affected.
deleteBusy: A query is running or connecting on it. Stop it first.

tunnel.name: Profile name
tunnel.nameHint: Connections refer to the profile by this name. It is saved as a tunnel file (.spelaion/tunnels/).
tunnel.fixedHint: When editing, the profile keeps its name and location: connections refer to it.
tunnel.agentKey: Only this key from the agent (optional)
tunnel.agentKeyPlaceholder: Empty: every key loaded in the agent

methodHints.agent: Uses the keys loaded in your SSH agent; choose one if the server limits authentication attempts.
methodHints.key: If the key has a passphrase, it is asked when connecting.
methodHints.password: Typed once to save it in the keychain, or asked each time.
methodHints.keyboard-interactive: For servers that ask questions such as a 2FA code: they are asked when connecting.
methodHints.custom: These methods are tried in order and kept as they are in the file.

tunnel.useProxy: Go through a SOCKS5 or HTTP proxy
tunnel.proxySavePassword: Save the proxy password in the keychain
tunnel.proxyHint: The first hop is reached through the proxy. SOCKS5 resolves the hop's name on the proxy's side.
tunnel.proxyAloneHint: Without hops, the proxy itself reaches the database: connections using this tunnel go through it.
tunnel.keepaliveHint: When a server sends nothing for that long, a keep-alive is sent, so a NAT or firewall does not drop an idle tunnel; after that many unanswered the tunnel is shown as down. Empty: 15 s and 3. 0 seconds sends none; 0 unanswered never gives up.
tunnel.connectTimeoutHint: How long each hop may take to answer before giving up. Empty: 15 s. Time spent typing a passphrase or a 2FA code does not count.

url.label: Or paste a connection URL
url.unsupported: This app has no driver for that database yet.

dbeaver.or: Or bring your connections from another client:
dbeaver.title: Import from DBeaver
dbeaver.savePasswords: Store the passwords DBeaver saved in the system keychain
dbeaver.passwordsHint: Otherwise SpelaionDB asks for them when connecting. Passwords are never written to the connection files. SSH tunnels and SOCKS proxies are imported too, as network profiles.

kubernetes.name: Resource name
kubernetes.noPorts: The resource declares no ports: type the port in the Main tab.
kubernetes.hint: SpelaionDB runs kubectl port-forward with your kubeconfig. The connection’s port is the port of this resource; the host in the Main tab is only used for TLS.
kubernetes.exclusive: A connection goes through Kubernetes or an SSH tunnel, not both.
kubernetes.mainHint: Through Kubernetes: the port is the resource’s, chosen in the Kubernetes tab.

cloudToken.awsRdsHint: Runs “aws rds generate-db-auth-token” on every connection: the AWS CLI must be signed in on this computer. Tokens last 15 minutes and need TLS.
cloudToken.azureAdHint: Runs “az account get-access-token” on every connection: the Azure CLI must be signed in on this computer. Use your Entra ID user as the user.
cloudToken.googleCloudSqlHint: Runs “gcloud sql generate-login-token” on every connection: the gcloud CLI must be signed in on this computer. Use your IAM user as the user.

copies.duplicated: “{{copy}}” is a copy of “{{name}}”, already saved. Its password will be asked when connecting. Change what differs, or close.
copies.duplicatedWithPassword: “{{copy}}” is a copy of “{{name}}”, already saved, with its own copy of the stored password. Change what differs, or close.
copies.copiedWithout: “{{name}}” copied, without its password. Left out: {{fields}}.
copies.pasted: “{{name}}” was pasted as a personal connection, already saved. Its password is asked when connecting. Check it, or close.
copies.pastedWithout: “{{name}}” was pasted as a personal connection, already saved. Its password is asked when connecting. Not taken from the clipboard: {{fields}}. Check it, or close.
copies.clipboardUnavailable: The clipboard could not be read: select a connection and press Ctrl+V.

move.title: Move {{name}} to a folder
move.personalHint: Its file moves inside your personal connections. Its stored password, filters and bookmarks go with it.
move.projectHint: Its file moves inside the repository's .spelaion/connections/: your team sees the move when you commit it. Its stored password, filters and bookmarks go with it.
move.folderHint: Nested folders with /, such as prod/eu. Empty for no folder.
move.inUse: Disconnect the tabs that use {{name}} before moving it.

engineChange.title: Engine change
engineChange.summary: Engine: {{from}} → {{to}}. Nothing is saved until you save.
engineChange.hint: The connection keeps its file, filters, bookmarks and history. Saving closes its open sessions: they belong to the old engine, and its tabs connect again when run.
